title: Qutrit entanglement and joint multi-parameter estimation in an optical clock platform
authors: Ohad Lib, Shuheng Liu, Maximilian Ammenwerth, Hendrik Timme, Shijia Sun, Qiongyi He, Marcus Huber, Giuseppe Vitagliano, Immanuel Bloch, Johannes Zeiher
abstract: Quantum metrology harnesses entanglement to improve measurement precision beyond classical limits. While standard protocols rely on two-level qubits to estimate a single parameter, extending them to entangled multi-level qudits enables the optimal simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters within a single probe. However, generating such multi-level entanglement and harnessing it for joint multi-parameter estimation in atomic clocks has remained an outstanding challenge. Here, we experimentally demonstrate genuine qutrit entanglement and joint multi-parameter estimation in an optical clock platform. Leveraging control over the ground state and two fine-structure clock states of $^{88}\text{Sr}$ atoms trapped in triple-magic optical tweezers, we generate a maximally entangled two-qutrit state with a loss-postselected fidelity of F = 0.85(1), certifying genuine multi-level entanglement. Taking advantage of this high-dimensional entanglement, we theoretically construct and experimentally realize an optimal two-qutrit metrological probe state and noise-robust readout circuit to simultaneously estimate injected phases on two optical clock transitions. We observe a joint estimation variance below the ideal individual two-level sensing threshold, and show theoretically that this advantage persists at state-of-the-art atom numbers under circuit-level noise. These results demonstrate the key building blocks towards quantum information science with high-dimensional states encoded in the internal energy levels of neutral atoms.
summary: The paper demonstrates how to use genuine qutrit entanglement in an optical atomic clock platform to simultaneously estimate multiple physical parameters. By leveraging the higher dimensionality of the internal atomic states, they surpass the precision limits achievable by treating each parameter estimation independently. This work establishes key building blocks for quantum information science using neutral atoms.
main_problem: The research addresses extending quantum metrology from single-parameter estimation (using qubits) to joint multi-parameter estimation using entangled multi-level qudits in an atomic clock platform.
main_result: They experimentally demonstrated genuine qutrit entanglement and achieved a joint estimation variance lower than the ideal individual two-level sensing threshold, showing this advantage persists under noise.
method: The authors used controlled operations (like CZ gates) to generate high-dimensional entangled states in $^{88}	ext{Sr}$ atoms and then employed optimal metrological probes and readout circuits for joint phase estimation.
model_or_system: The physical system is an optical clock platform using $^{88}	ext{Sr}$ atoms trapped in triple-magic optical tweezers. The internal energy levels form a qutrit ($\{|0angle, |1angle, |2angle\}$), allowing for the encoding of higher-dimensional quantum information.
key_observables: Joint estimation variance ($Y_{	ext{joint}}$), entanglement fidelity ($F$), and comparison against individual two-level sensing thresholds.
important_parameters: The number of atoms ($N$), the injected phases ($	heta_1, 	heta_2$), and noise parameters (e.g., coherence factors $\eta$).
main_assumptions: The fidelity calculation is not fully corrected for all state preparation and measurement errors; theoretical analysis often assumes specific noise models (depolarizing/dephasing).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, demonstrate entanglement via population measurements ($P_{ii}$) and parity oscillations ($	ext{C}_{ij}$), and compare joint vs. individual estimation variances under ideal and noisy conditions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical platform and generating qutrit entanglement to theoretically constructing optimal multi-parameter probes, experimentally realizing the joint estimation, and finally analyzing noise robustness across different theoretical limits.
why_interesting: This work directly pushes the boundaries of quantum sensing by moving beyond qubit limitations into high-dimensional qudit systems using neutral atoms, which is a major focus area in AMO physics and quantum metrology.
